land.text: the Wei River valley, evacuated by the Zhou court after the sack of Fenghao in 771 (Western Zhou page)

predecessors.note: The zhou-dynasty dossier (ea-01-a) carries the matching loss at 771 with counterpart Quanrong.

land.text: 'the former Zhou land' the Rong occupied until Duke Wen of Qin's victory of 750; Qin kept the part west of Qishan

successors.note: The page says Duke Wen 'returned the territory east of Qishan to Zhou, and kept the rest for Qin'; the qin dossier carries gains from Quanrong at 770 and 750.

capitals.note: 'The traditional base is modern Wēiróng Town in Jingning County, Gansu'; the page names no capital and the Quanrong were not a city-based state: one dot for the traditional base.

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe (Cliopatria lacks the Quanrong). The page has no infobox and no area; 'active in the northwestern part of China during and after the Zhou dynasty'. The shape is the researcher's reading: the evacuated Wei valley plus a 60 km disc at Jingning.

region.text: the Wei River valley the Zhou court evacuated in 771 ('the former Zhou land') and the traditional Quanrong base, 'modern Wēiróng Town in Jingning County, Gansu'

ledger.note: 771: the Quanrong, invited by the Marquess of Shen, storm the Zhou capital. 'In 771 BCE, the Marquess of Shen invited the Quanrong to join him in an attack on King You of Zhou. The joint force subsequently occupied the Zhōu capital Haojing, killing King You and capturing his concubine Bao Si.' The page gives no founding date (King Mu's campaign is undated), so 771 is the first dated event and the shape after it is a reading.

region.text: 'the land west of Qishan' that King Ping promised Qin on condition that Qin expel the Rong

ledger.note: 766: Duke Xiang of Qin dies fighting the Quanrong at Qishan. 'In 766 BC, the 12th year of his reign, Duke Xiang died while campaigning against the' Quanrong, in Qishan; 'King Ping further promised to give Qin the land west of Qishan' if Qin expelled the Rong 'occupying it' (undated; the war's start is undated, 766 is the first dated campaign).

region.text: 'the land west of Qishan' that King Ping promised Qin on condition that Qin expel the Rong

ledger.note: 750: Duke Wen of Qin breaks the Rong. 'In 750 BC he defeated the Rong tribes that were occupying the former Zhou land.'

region.text: the Wei River valley the Zhou court evacuated in 771 ('the former Zhou land') and the traditional Quanrong base, 'modern Wēiróng Town in Jingning County, Gansu'

ledger.note: 750: the Rong lose the Wei valley to Qin. 'In 750 BC he defeated the Rong tribes that were occupying the former Zhou land'; 'He returned the territory east of Qishan to Zhou, and kept the rest for Qin.' The page says 'Rong tribes', not Quanrong by name, and the Jingning base is not mentioned.

region.text: the Wei River valley the Zhou court evacuated in 771 ('the former Zhou land') and the traditional Quanrong base, 'modern Wēiróng Town in Jingning County, Gansu'

ledger.note: 750: the Rong hold of the Wei valley ends, and with it this dossier. The page gives no end to the Quanrong as a people ('the page does not describe a final fate'); 750 is the last date at which any page opened shows them holding land.

wars.name: Sack of Fenghao

zones.text: the Zhou capital Fenghao (Fengjing and Haojing) and the Wei valley

wars.outcome: The rebel Marquis of Shen, Zeng and the Quanrong defeated King You's army at Mount Li and sacked the capital; the king was killed and the court moved east, ending the Western Zhou.
wars.note: Duke Xiang of Qin 'sent an army to assist the Zhou' (Quanrong page) and escorted King Ping to Luoyi (Duke Xiang page). The Quanrong page adds that 'the invaders left after taking a tribute from the Zhou and stealing the Nine Tripod Cauldrons', which does not say they stayed in the valley; the Duke Wen page does say Rong occupied the former Zhou land until 750.

wars.name: Qin wars against the Rong

zones.text: 'the land west of Qishan' that King Ping promised Qin on condition that Qin expel the Rong

wars.outcome: Qin, 'the westernmost of the Zhou states, bore the brunt of the fighting against the Rong'; Duke Xiang died fighting the Quanrong at Qishan in 766, and Duke Wen defeated the Rong occupying the former Zhou land in 750, keeping the land west of Qishan.
wars.note: Years: 766 from the Duke Xiang page, 750 from the Duke Wen page; the war's beginning is undated on both.

certainty.note: No Quanrong boundary is on any page; the Qishan line is the only named limit and is soft.

notes: Pages opened (4 of up to 5): Quanrong, Western Zhou, Duke Xiang of Qin, Duke Wen of Qin. Wikidata id left null (unreachable). WHAT THIS IS: not a founded state but the Rong hold of the Wei valley between the 771 sack and Duke Wen's 750 victory, plus the traditional base at Jingning; FAMILY steppe (the colour agent may choose). START -771 and END -750 are the first and last dates the pages tie to the Rong holding land; the Quanrong page says they left Haojing after taking tribute and is silent on the valley, the Western Zhou page is silent on who held it, and only the Duke Wen page says 'Rong tribes' occupied 'the former Zhou land' (not the Quanrong by name): so the 771-750 hold is confidence 2 and the dissolve 1. The zhou-dynasty dossier's 771 loss, the qin dossier's 770 and 750 gains and this one fit together; the qin 770 gain (the promise of the land west of Qishan) is a promise, not a holding, on the Duke Xiang page. The Duke Wen page says Qin 'returned the territory east of Qishan to Zhou', which the qin and eastern-zhou dossiers do not show. AREA: none. The Xianyun, Xirong and other Rong are separate or overlapping names (see xianyun). Not used: the Quanrong page's later passages (Han tribute, Tang petition).
